Senior design · Industrial automation

Dodge Industrial Automation Cell

A multi-stage automation cell concept for handling flange and sprocket parts. My work focuses on the flange hopper and transfer cart, along with actuator sizing and system interfaces.

Project status
In progress
My focus
Hopper, cart, sizing & controls interfaces
Engineering areas
Mechanical design · Pneumatics · Automation
01 / Context

Project objective

Develop an automation cell concept that handles flange and sprocket components through a sequence of material handling and production operations. The system includes a flange hopper, part transfer, heating and stamping operations, assembly, and controls.

The current design basis includes 16 flange sizes, a 100-part hopper capacity, and a target throughput of 75 parts per hour. Flanges are stamped at a shared heater and stamping station.

02 / Design process

Subsystem development

The flange subsystem is being developed around reliable single-part feeding and repeatable movement between work locations.

  • Explore a bottom-fed hopper with adjustable separators for the flange size range.
  • Develop a magnetic transfer cart running on a Festo linear rail.
  • Size pneumatic separators and electric actuators against the part and motion requirements.
  • Plan sensor, PLC, power, and network interfaces for integration with the larger cell.
